brief: UBS prime brokerage flow note. Hedge funds favoured quality AI compute over funding-sensitive Neoclouds: following CoreWeave's (CRWV) results, funds used the Neocloud rebound to add more than one standard deviation of shorts, reflecting funding concerns and Democrats' scrutiny of data centres, while adding 1.7 standard deviations to Hyperscaler longs, favouring higher-quality companies with established compute capacity and lower policy exposure. In the US, Capital Goods was the most net-sold sector for the week, followed by Software (-0.8std for the week, -2.5std on Friday alone) and Biotech (-2.2std over the week). In Europe, Healthcare was the most-bought sector, extending a defensive rotation underway since late October, while funds kept selling the ex-AI economy, with Low Quality and Cyclicals the most net-sold factors, concentrated in Tech and Software. Since 5 November, European long/short and quant strategies have rebounded 2.1% and 1.4% respectively on strength in Semis, Capital Goods and Banks, UBS's three largest hedge fund net exposures, recovering 75% of October's drawdown. US and APAC strategies remain under pressure after a difficult October, though quant performance there has started improving since 11 November.
